briefs.source_chain: Waller signals disinflation and floats holding rates → 10yr yields ease 3bp → alongside a strong ISM Services print (vs. an earlier ISM Manufacturing decline) and a bifurcated SNOW-up/AVGO-down earnings reaction, GS stays Buy on AVGO → desk stays constructive into Friday's payrolls (GS forecasts 40k).
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain: Waller dovish lean eases yields → strong ISM Services vs. weak Manufacturing plus SNOW beat/AVGO miss-guide → Goldman stays Buy → payrolls Friday, GS forecasts 40k.

distortions.what: "Goldman stays Buy" is placed right after both SNOW and AVGO are mentioned; source states the Buy rating specifically and only for AVGO ("We remain Buy-rated on the stock" in the AVGO paragraph). A reader could momentarily read it as covering both names.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — correctly read in context it still resolves to AVGO=Buy, which is the source's actual call; no SNOW rating is asserted either way.

briefs.source_chain: Low-volume tape holds gains on AI-supportive datapoints → Broadcom's FY27/28 AI revenue guide (Anthropic largest FY27 custom-silicon customer, OpenAI/Meta material FY28) justifies GS staying buyers and raising target to $540 from $525 despite an in-line-to-soft Q4 guide → GS stays modestly pro-risk (OW equities, UW credit) as earnings growth outruns bonds/credit → desk logs Iran/Kuwait, EU gas, CLARITY Act and French fiscal risk as separate watch items, with CAC 40 still not investable.
briefs.brief_chain: Same: AI-supportive tape on low volume → Broadcom's FY27 guide (Anthropic/OpenAI/Meta) plus 12x FY28 EPS valuation drives GS buyers stance and $540 target raise → GS stays tactically neutral 3m / pro-risk 12m, OW equities / UW credit → reports Iran, EU gas, CLARITY Act, and CAC 40 without further argument.

distortions.what: Allocation line drops "Neutral bonds, commodities and cash" from the source's fuller asset-allocation stance, keeping only OW equities / UW credit.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the omitted legs are Neutral, i.e. no active call; dropping them doesn't change any position.

distortions.what: Iran item is compressed to "Iran struck US bases in Kuwait," dropping Trump's threat of further strikes and the reported 19 Iranian deaths from the prior bombardment.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — this is a reported-without-argument geopolitical headline in both source and brief; no trade or stance is attached to it either way.

distortions.what: Brief omits several source items entirely: Meta's Muse Spark 1.3 release, the Schneider/Tony P podcast blurb, the Trump $1 coin note, the Quote of the Day, the EU Nat Gas Consumers/Power Price Sensitive Utilities baskets, and the Stat/Chart of the Day.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — none of these carry a stance, level, or call in the source; they are digest filler the brief's own framing ("reports most of its content") signals as compressed.

briefs.source_chain: Soft ADP plus Williams' pushback ease rates ahead of Waller/NFP → Privorotsky reads the recent hawkish tone as Warsh preserving credibility, not a committee shift → collapsing cost-per-token forces consumption to outrun price declines or compute oversupply becomes plausible, which with credit repricing explains the AI de-rating (Broadcom Q4 miss-vs-huge-bar against a strong FY27/28 guide, cleaner Snowflake) → Iran read is escalate-to-de-escalate with oil near the top of its range → core view: markets stable/higher as long as energy doesn't rise, with an open question on whether AI equities can finally re-rate on good news.
briefs.brief_chain: Same core chain: soft ADP/Williams ease rates into Waller/NFP → Warsh-credibility read on the hawkish tone → token-price compression outrunning demand growth makes compute oversupply plausible and explains the de-rating (Broadcom miss vs. guide, cleaner Snowflake) → escalate-to-de-escalate on Iran, oil near top of range → markets stable/higher unless energy rises.

distortions.what: Drops "(although Korean memory has faded)" from the overnight markets line and softens "His last comments were genuinely two-sided" plus "I think the way he frames the argument could shift pricing for September" down to a plainer "room to lean dovish."
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the directional read (room to lean dovish) survives; the dropped nuance is texture, not a changed conviction or condition.

distortions.what: Omits the WSJ sourcing behind the Iran call (Trump privately weighing declaring the war over, the Hormuz Strait quote) and the Risk-section discussion of whether AI equities can finally re-rate on good Broadcom/Snowflake news, plus the Ag/sugar-futures side-note.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the brief keeps the resulting calls (escalate-to-de-escalate, energy near top of range, stable/higher core view) intact; the omitted material is supporting color and an unresolved open question, not a stance or level.

briefs.source_chain: Silicon Data's token-expenditure index fell 29% in August to ~$0.97/M tokens (>50% off the May peak) while JPMorgan data shows OpenRouter volume +47% vs. spend +7% and H100 rental falling → volume isn't paying for the price cut, and absent a capability jump (Astra, unlaunched) compute oversupply is plausible → that collides with heavy financed hyperscaler capex (~$737bn, 38% of revenue) that credit is already repricing (78/91 2026 hyperscaler bonds below issue) → equity multiples are the lagging indicator of the AI de-rating; three counterarguments don't rescue multiples; separately GS's Schneider reiterates Buy on Broadcom.
briefs.brief_chain: Same: token price compression (Silicon Data -29%, ~$0.97/M, >50% off May peak) outrunning volume growth (JPM: OpenRouter volume +47% vs. spend +7%, H100 rental falling) → absent a capability jump (unlaunched Astra) compute oversupply is plausible → collides with financed hyperscaler capex (~$737bn, 38% of revenue), already repriced by credit (78/91 bonds below issue) → three counterarguments listed, none rescuing multiples; separately Schneider reiterates Buy on Broadcom.

distortions.what: Omits the article's ROIC arithmetic chain (cheaper tokens → inference revenue falls while depreciation/interest ramp → ROIC collapses → multiple prices a utility with stranded useful life) and the on-device/local-inference structural argument.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — this is elaboration on the same de-rating thesis the brief already states; dropping it doesn't change the stance, the invalidation (Astra), or the figures.

briefs.source_chain: Hyperscalers (Amazon) absorb higher memory costs rather than cut orders, signaling memory suppliers retain pricing power → yet memory equities have lagged, consolidating between trend lines (Micron the strongest, closing above its 50-day; Samsung/Hynix pinned at support, Hynix's 50-day well above spot) → with Korean retail speculation cooled and KOSPI vol crushed, a break higher could trigger an aggressive catch-up squeeze, playable via KOSPI upside convexity.
briefs.brief_chain: Same: Amazon capex-cost signal shows memory pricing power → memory equities have lagged, consolidating (DRAM ETF above its 21-day MA; Micron strongest, above its 50-day, $1,000 close as trigger; Samsung/Hynix pinned at support, Hynix's 50-day well above price) → cooled Korean speculation and crushed KOSPI vol set up a possible catch-up squeeze via KOSPI upside convexity.
